feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is claimed for it. Iteration 0 (baseline) finished the oval 20/20 but went off track on the s-bend (0.17) and slalom (0.12) at max_error about 0.061 m. Iteration 1 (wide array, 0.10 m track, 0.5 kg, 0.033 m radius) dropped the oval to 17/20 and raised oscillation to 0.26, while bends gained only to 0.24 and 0.19. Iteration 2 (wide array, baseline drivetrain, 0.5 kg) gave oval 15/20 with oscillation 0.21 and bends of 0.20 and 0.12, so the wide array alone did not clearly help. I kept the baseline controller so that only geometry changes, and I moved the sensors forward to test look-ahead. Next race: if the oval finishes near 20/20 and bend progress rises above 0.17 and 0.12, keep y=0.07 and then test a modest spread increase. If progress is unchanged with max_error still near 0.06, change the footprint rather than the lead. If the oval loses finishes, the lead is adding lag, so return y toward 0.06.
requested_changes: If the s-bend or slalom still end off track with line_loss_events of 1 or more and max_error near 0.06 m, change sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016 with the y=0.07 row unchanged. Iterations 0 and 2 both show bend failure at the limit, so footprint coverage is the next untested lever.

If bend progress rises clearly above 0.17 and 0.12 while the oval stays at 20/20, change x to plus or minus 0.032 m at 16 mm pitch and keep mass at 0.6 kg. Iteration 1 gave a partial bend gain from the wider array, and the mass was never isolated from the 0.5 kg drivetrain.

If the oval stops finishing (below 18/20) with oscillation above 0.2, move the sensor row back to y=0.06 to cut lag. Iteration 2 showed the wide array with lighter drivetrain hurt oval stability, so lead may add the same kind of lag.
